page.title: Today
page.purpose: Answer 'what should I eat next, and what do I do?' with the next uncompleted meal, a calculation-backed reason, honest unknown states, and a one-action easy-night alternative.

priorities.statement: The next meal to eat, with its calculation-backed reason, leads before any supporting detail.
Energy, protein, portion cost, and effort each carry their own known or unknown state rather than a fabricated zero.
The easy-night alternative is one action away and is scoped to the selected future occurrence, never to history.
Planned and recorded intake stay visibly separate and a dinner-only plan never claims full-day compliance.
An empty or incomplete plan is described honestly with a recovery action instead of a filled-slot badge.

states.description: The surface at rest with data present; the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
First read of the page's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
The read succeeded and there is genuinely nothing, which is distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing data could not be read; what is missing is named rather than shown as zero.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
The request failed; the reason and the next available action are stated.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified next to it.
A write is in flight; the affected control says why it is unavailable.
The client cannot reach the API; read-only or queued behavior is explained.
No recipe satisfies the active required rules; the page names the conflict and offers Add a meal or Review restrictions without relaxing a rule.
One or more contributing prices are missing; the cost is shown as a known subtotal plus unpriced items, never as a complete total.
A metric is unavailable because a quantity, price, or nutrient value is missing while the meal itself remains usable.
The 'What sounds better?' dialog is open with reason chips and eligible alternatives for the selected occurrence.
The selected occurrence has already been recorded as eaten, so the next slot is offered instead of editing history.

elements.name: Next meal
elements.description: The meal the person should eat next, with its context and actions.
The selected meal's readable name and local date/slot context.
A concise, calculation-backed reason such as 'Uses your opened rice; 6 minutes of active prep.'
Energy for the selected scope, with its own unknown state.
Protein for the selected scope, with its own unknown state.
Allocated portion cost for the selected scope, with its own unknown state.
Active preparation time and effort, kept distinct from elapsed cooking time.
States which metric is unknown and why, so a missing value is never read as zero.

elements.name: Let's make it
elements.description: The one dominant action to begin the selected meal.

elements.name: Swap meal
elements.description: Opens the effort-aware swap for the selected future occurrence.

elements.name: Not a cooking kind of night?
elements.description: The one-action entry to a low-effort swap scoped to the selected meal.

elements.name: What sounds better?
elements.description: Reason chips and up to four useful eligible alternatives.
Candidate alternatives, each with name, active time, known metrics, and a short reason.
Something different, Less effort, Lower cost, and Missing ingredients; no reason is mandatory.
Explains that the meal remains usable while specific data is unknown.
Rule-conflict summary with counts and no automatic relaxation of a restriction.
States that the occurrence is already recorded and points at the next slot.

claims.statement: The next meal carries a calculation-backed reason drawn from the evaluated result, not a restated ingredient list.
Each of energy, protein, portion cost, and effort reports its own known or unknown state, and an unknown value is never rendered as zero.
A meal with an unpriced item is perceivably different from a meal with a known zero cost, because the two support opposite conclusions.
Beginning the meal is the one visually dominant action, with swap and easy-night alternatives subordinate.
The easy-night swap is reachable in one action, scoped to the selected future occurrence, and prevents editing a consumed occurrence.
When no meal satisfies the required rules the page names the conflict and offers recovery actions, and never relaxes a restriction to produce a recommendation.
An already eaten occurrence is reported as recorded and the next slot is offered instead of a replacement for history.
The swap and easy-night controls are keyboard reachable and the dialog returns focus to its trigger on close.
The next meal and its primary action are visible at phone width without scrolling past an analytics panel.
The Today page never scrolls the whole document sideways at any supported viewport.
A meal with incomplete data stays usable and the page says what is missing rather than blocking on completeness.
